prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1432; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound in the left lane when the vehicle drifted across the center line and struck the front of an oncoming vehicle operated by Driver 2. The impact was low speed but direct, and both vehicles came to rest in the roadway. Driver 1 remained in the driver's seat until responding units arrived and reported pain in the left knee. A passenger in the front seat of Driver 1's vehicle was also present and was checked at the scene. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred just as described by Driver 1, and two independent witnesses on the shoulder gave consistent accounts. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front bumper, hood, and grille of Driver 1's vehicle and matching damage to the front end of Driver 2's vehicle, consistent with a head-on contact at the reported point of impact. Officers found no evidence of prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the registration and policy documents presented at the scene. Driver 1 was transported by ambulance for evaluation of the knee injury, which appeared consistent with the forces involved in this collision.
